claims.statement: Tamoxifen citrate is FDA-approved for metastatic breast cancer in women and men; for adjuvant treatment of node-positive breast cancer in postmenopausal women following total mastectomy or segmental mastectomy, axillary dissection and breast irradiation; for adjuvant treatment of axillary-node-negative breast cancer in women following those same surgical and radiation procedures; for reduction in the risk of invasive breast cancer in women with ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) following breast surgery and radiation, which is a risk-reduction purpose and not treatment of existing DCIS; and for reduction in the incidence of breast cancer in women at high risk, where the cited label defines high risk as women at least 35 years of age with a 5-year predicted breast cancer risk of at least 1.67% by the Gail model. The incidence-reduction indication is limited to those high-risk women and to women with DCIS. LABEL CURRENCY: this list is taken from a single labeler's 2007 tablet SPL (Andrx, setid 8f642753-9e12-433c-a0bc-ab33dac41ddf). The currently maintained Soltamox tamoxifen citrate oral solution SPL (Mayne Pharma, version 2, published 2021-12-01, setid 1e6ff055-590c-41e6-9530-1fdf04cdbd02) restricts the metastatic and adjuvant indications to adults with ER-positive breast cancer; that restriction is absent from the 2007 tablet SPL, so the 2007 wording must not be presented as the current labeled scope.

context.population: metastatic: women and men. Node-positive adjuvant: postmenopausal women, postoperative. Node-negative adjuvant: women, postoperative. Risk reduction: women with DCIS, and high-risk women at least 35 years of age. The current Soltamox SPL restricts metastatic and adjuvant use to ER-positive adults.

claims.statement: The tamoxifen citrate label carries a boxed warning for serious and sometimes fatal uterine malignancies, stroke and pulmonary embolism, and its scope covers BOTH women taking tamoxifen to reduce the incidence of breast cancer in the high-risk setting AND women with ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS). On the 2007 Andrx tablet SPL the boxed warning reports, per 1,000 women-years: endometrial adenocarcinoma 2.20 on tamoxifen versus 0.71 on placebo; uterine sarcoma 0.17 versus 0.04; stroke 1.43 versus 1.00; and pulmonary embolism 0.75 versus 0.25. These comparisons do not share one denominator or one observation window and must not be combined. The uterine rates come from updated NSABP P-1 follow-up at a median of 6.9 years and derive from 53 versus 17 endometrial adenocarcinomas among the 8,306 women who had an intact uterus at randomization. The stroke and pulmonary embolism rates come from an earlier data cut-off at approximately 4.2 years median follow-up over the full randomized denominators of 6,681 women on tamoxifen and 6,707 on placebo, with 18 versus 6 pulmonary embolism events. All are rates per 1,000 women-years, not percentages and not risks per 1,000 randomized women. The label's stroke rate ratio has a confidence interval crossing 1, so the numerically higher stroke rate is not a demonstrated statistically significant increase. LABEL CURRENCY: the boxed warning is reworded on the currently maintained Soltamox SPL (version 2, published 2021-12-01); that current wording has not been retrieved and is not anchored in this packet, so the 2007 text must not be presented as the current boxed warning.

claims.statement: Tamoxifen is contraindicated in patients with known hypersensitivity to tamoxifen or its ingredients. In addition, for the risk-reduction indications specifically - which on the cited label means BOTH reduction in breast cancer incidence in high-risk women AND women with ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) - tamoxifen is contraindicated in women who require concomitant coumarin-type anticoagulant therapy and in women with a history of deep vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolus. claims.statement: Labeled clinical-trial dosing for tamoxifen was NOT uniformly 20 mg/day. The cited label's Dosage and Administration section attributes distinct protocols to named trials: ECOG and NATO used 10 mg twice daily for two years; the Toronto trial used 10 mg three times daily for two years; and NSABP B-14 used 10 mg twice daily for at least five years. For patients with breast cancer that label's recommended daily dose is 20 to 40 mg, with doses above 20 mg/day given in divided doses morning and evening. The 20 mg/day for five years regimen is what the label specifies for DCIS and for reduction of breast cancer incidence in high-risk women, and it is the NSABP P-1 prevention protocol; it is not the protocol of every trial underlying the approved uses. Tablet strengths on this label are expressed as tamoxifen-equivalent doses, so 20 mg of tamoxifen corresponds to 30.4 mg of tamoxifen citrate. This is historical label and trial-protocol context from a 2007 SPL, not a use recommendation, and it must not be read as a current or universal adjuvant duration; the label predates the extended-duration evidence recorded in tamoxifen-efficacy-atlas-extended-001.

claims.statement: In the NSABP P-1 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled prevention trial in women at increased breast cancer risk, tamoxifen 20 mg/day reduced the cumulative incidence of invasive breast cancer by 49% (43.4 per 1,000 women on placebo vs. 22.0 per 1,000 on tamoxifen through 69 months) and reduced estrogen-receptor-positive tumor incidence by 69%, but this benefit came with an increased rate of endometrial cancer (risk ratio 2.53) and elevated rates of stroke, pulmonary embolism, and deep-vein thrombosis, particularly in women aged 50 and older. The cited label reports a SEPARATE analysis of the same trial: a 44% reduction in invasive breast cancer incidence (86 versus 156 cases) at a median follow-up of 4.2 years, and 33 versus 14 endometrial cancers, RR 2.48 (95% CI 1.27-4.92). RR 2.53 (95% CI 1.35-4.97) is the primary publication's own figure and RR 2.48 is the label's separate analysis over a different analysis set and data cut-off; the two are recorded unmerged and must never be averaged, reconciled into one number, or presented as versions of a single estimate. The same applies to the eligibility threshold: the primary states it as a 5-year predicted risk of at least 1.66% while the label states 1.67%; both are recorded and neither replaces the other.

claims.statement: In ATLAS (Davies C, Pan H, Godwin J, et al., Lancet 2013;381:805-816), women with breast cancer who had completed about five years of adjuvant tamoxifen were randomised to continue to 10 years or to stop at 5 years. The primary's own time-to-event estimates for years 5 to 14 after diagnosis, in the ER-POSITIVE EFFICACY POPULATION (3,428 continue versus 3,418 stop), are: cumulative recurrence risk 21.4% versus 25.1%, an absolute reduction of 3.7 percentage points; cumulative breast cancer mortality 12.2% versus 15.0%, an absolute reduction of 2.8 percentage points. Over the whole reported follow-up that same population recorded 617 versus 711 recurrences (log-rank rate ratio 0.84, 95% CI 0.76-0.94, p=0.002), 639 versus 722 deaths from ANY cause (rate ratio 0.87, 95% CI 0.78-0.97, p=0.01), and 331 versus 397 deaths with recurrence (rate ratio 0.83). Against that benefit, in the SEPARATE SAFETY POPULATION - any ER status, and excluding women with a hysterectomy recorded at trial entry, who were 17-18% of the cohort - cumulative endometrial cancer risk for years 5 to 14 was 3.1% versus 1.6% (116 versus 63 events; rate ratio 1.74, 95% CI 1.30-2.34, p=0.0002), with cumulative endometrial cancer mortality 0.4% versus 0.2%. Three boundaries must be kept. First, the crude event proportions (recurrence 18.0% versus 20.8%; any death 18.6% versus 21.1%) are counts over the efficacy-population denominators, NOT cumulative risks. That distinction is what understated the harm here: the crude endometrial proportions, roughly 2.15% versus 1.19% once the trial-entry hysterectomies the primary excludes are taken out, understate the years-5-to-14 cumulative endometrial cancer risk of 3.1% versus 1.6% by roughly 1.7-fold, and the 1.80% versus 0.97% figures this packet previously carried were further understated because they were computed over the full randomisation denominators. Second, the rate ratios are log-rank estimates and are not derived from those crude proportions, so the two must never be paired as though one produced the other. Third, the efficacy population and the safety population are different denominators and must not be mixed; the deaths-with-recurrence row is likewise not identical to the paper's methods-defined breast cancer mortality analysis and must not be substituted for it. The extended-duration benefit and the endometrial cancer risk must always be presented together and never in isolation.

claims.statement: Tamoxifen (Nolvadex) is widely marketed and self-administered in bodybuilding and anabolic-androgenic-steroid (AAS) communities as unsupervised post-cycle therapy (PCT) to restore endogenous testosterone and manage gynecomastia after steroid cycles, although no evidence-based clinical guideline supports that specific use and no controlled human trial in this packet establishes its efficacy or safety. The 2025 Frontiers in Chemistry paper cited here is a LABORATORY COMPOSITION ANALYSIS of 601 police-seized performance-enhancing-drug samples collected January 2020 to August 2024 and tested at the Polish Official Medicines Control Laboratory; it is not a patient survey and reports no patient outcomes. Of 63 samples declaring PCT drugs, seven declared tamoxifen: five contained the declared active ingredient and two were incorrectly labeled, one containing EDTA disodium salt dihydrate and one containing no active ingredient. Tamoxifen was additionally identified as an UNDECLARED active ingredient in seven further samples. This is a selected seized-product sample and does not estimate the composition of the illicit tamoxifen supply generally. The adverse-event percentages sometimes attributed to this paper - decreased libido and erectile dysfunction 24%, acne 21%, fatigue 19%, mood disorders 13%, visual disturbances 5%, arthralgia 4%, insomnia 4%, hot flushes 2% - are NOT its results: they appear in its Introduction, citing Rochoy et al. 2022, an analysis of self-reported bodybuilding-forum posts covering clomiphene and tamoxifen together. They are self-reported forum observations, not tamoxifen-specific incidence measured in any clinical cohort. A product-integrity risk and an efficacy/safety evidence gap are both real here, and both are distinct from the FDA-approved, prescription, pharmacy-dispensed product.

conflicts.summary: Extending adjuvant tamoxifen from 5 to 10 years (ATLAS) reduces breast cancer recurrence and mortality but increases endometrial cancer incidence; the benefit and the risk must always be presented together and never in isolation. UPDATED 2026-09-07: the reconciliation this conflict called for is done. The primary Lancet report is now anchored in this packet, the claim leads with the primary's years-5-to-14 cumulative risk estimates, the efficacy and safety populations are stated distinctly, and the exclusion of women with a hysterectomy recorded at trial entry is stated. The conflict stays open for two reasons. First, the benefit-and-risk presentation constraint is a permanent rendering rule rather than something a review can discharge. Second, the endometrial cancer safety assertion embedded in this efficacy claim still has no eligible A1/A2 source in this packet: no regulator label here reports ATLAS, and the cited 2007 SPL predates it and reports the earlier NSABP B-14 conclusion against continuation beyond five years.

Popular online marketing frames tamoxifen (Nolvadex) as a bodybuilding PCT/gynecomastia agent, while the only FDA-approved, evidence-backed uses are breast cancer treatment, DCIS, and risk reduction in high-risk women; no controlled human trial evidence in this packet establishes efficacy or safety for unsupervised post-cycle testosterone recovery.

RESOLVED 2026-09-07 by anchoring the primary. The secondary trial-summary page cited for ATLAS labels the 18.6% versus 21.1% comparison (RR 0.87) as breast cancer mortality. The primary Lancet report (PMID 23219286), now added to this packet as pmc3596060-atlas-davies-2013-primary, labels that row "Any death" - all-cause mortality in the ER-positive efficacy population, 639 versus 722 of 3,428 versus 3,418 - and reports years-5-to-14 cumulative breast cancer mortality separately as 12.2% versus 15.0%. The claim now states the endpoints as the primary defines them and takes no figure from the secondary summary; that summary's quotes are retained in extractedEvidence solely as a record of what the page says. Residual limitation, not a reason to reopen: the 2026-09-07 re-review could not reach the secondary page (HTTP 403), so the mislabel finding itself rests on the 2026-09-05 retrieval.
